records.name: Philadelphia Front Runners
records.summary: An LGBTQIA+ running and walking club for athletes and allies at every pace. Members meet on Saturday mornings at Lloyd Hall on Boathouse Row for a run or walk at their own speed.
records.what_you_do: Run or walk at your own pace with the group on Saturday mornings, then talk with other members.

schedule.text: Every Saturday, 9:40 to 10:40 am, a run or walk at your own pace.

first_step.how: Go to Lloyd Hall on Boathouse Row on a Saturday morning, or join the group's mailing list through the join form on its website first.
first_step.basis: The group's site welcomes all running abilities and walkers, the calendar listing says open to all paces, and the site has a join form to start.
first_step.what_to_expect: The listed session runs one hour, from 9:40 to 10:40 am, and you choose a 1, 3 or 5 mile route or walk it at your own speed. Members of all paces take part, and the listing says it is free. The group usually goes to brunch at Little Pete's afterward.
first_visit_tips: Look at the 1, 3 or 5 mile routes on the group's Strava club page before you come.
Plan to arrive for the 9:40 am start at Lloyd Hall.
Stay for brunch afterward if you want to talk with members; the group usually goes to Little Pete's.

records.notes: The group's own site carries a 2018 copyright and dated posts only from 2017 and 2018, so it reads as out of date. Its Saturday start (9:30 am) conflicts with the Oct 10, 2026 calendar listing (9:40 am); the record uses the listing. The site also names a Monday 7 pm run at William Way Community Center, which no current source confirmed, so it is not recorded; William Way is in leads_only.

records.name: Philadelphia Gay Men's Chorus
records.summary: A men's chorus that performs concerts, does outreach with students, and takes bookings for events, with a focus on LGBTQ+ acceptance. It seeks tenor, baritone and bass singers, and has a separate dancers page.
records.what_you_do: Audition to sing tenor, baritone or bass (about 5 minutes, one on one with the director), or ask the volunteer contact about helping out. You can also come to a concert or the 80s Prom Night fundraiser, or become a member or donor.

schedule.text: Singer auditions are held twice a year, in August and December. Concert dates are not listed on the home page, so check the chorus site before you plan a visit.

locations.label: Philadelphia Youth Choral Ensembles Building (audition location)

cost.text: The audition page mentions no audition fee. Concert ticket prices are not shown on the home page.

first_step.how: Book a singer audition through the link on the audition page, which opens a few weeks before each round, or email membership@pgmc.org to ask for the next date.
first_step.basis: Anyone who sings tenor, baritone or bass can book an audition, but the site does not say whether visitors can sit in on rehearsals.
first_step.what_to_expect: An audition is one on one with the director and takes about 5 minutes. You do range and pitch exercises, sing a familiar song the director picks, and then sing your part from a piece you probably do not know. The page says you do not need a prepared piece.
first_visit_tips: You need basic note names, sharps, flats and time signatures, but you do not need to read music perfectly.
When you book, give your name and a phone number or email, and write again if you have no reply within about a week.
The audition page gives no parking or transit details, so ask when you book.

records.notes: The volunteer pages (pgmc.org/volunteer and pgmc.org/get-involved) returned 404, so roles for non-singers are not confirmed. The audition page points non-singers to dancing or to volunteer@pgmc.org. The audition dates (Aug 18 to 20) carry no year and are not used. The audition page gives membership@pgmc.org for bookings; info@pgmc.org stays as the record's one contact email. The Philadelphia Youth Choral Ensembles, which hosts the building, is in leads_only.

records.name: Philadelphia Girls Rowing Club
records.summary: A women's rowing club on Boathouse Row that trains adult novices in a yearly program and pairs each new rower with a mentor.
records.what_you_do: Learn to row on machines and then on the river, pass a skills and safety test, and help with the club's main fundraiser, the Braxton Regatta.

schedule.text: A yearly novice training program. An information session for applicants is held once a year in late April. Class dates are not listed.

cost.text: The adult novice program costs $950 in total: $600 in dues and a $350 initiation fee, due on the first day of training.

first_step.how: Email pgrcmembers14@gmail.com with 'ATTN: Membership Chair' in the title, saying why you want to join, your rowing background and how you could help the club.
first_step.basis: Applicants write a letter or email, may be invited to a spring information session, and pay a fixed fee, so the way in is clear but not open to walk-ins.
first_step.what_to_expect: If you are invited, you attend the information session, then train on rowing machines before moving to the river. The program ends with a skills and safety test and a mentor for the year. It is physical work: you lift and carry boats, get in and out of them, and must be able to swim.
first_visit_tips: Include your home address, email and phone number in your letter, since the club asks for them.
Be ready to pay the $950 novice fee on the first day of training.
Be a confident swimmer, since the club says you must be able to swim if a boat flips.

records.notes: The how-to-join page gives the fee, physical requirements and application steps, but no program length, no start date and no information session year (the session is late April, year not shown). The Adult Rowing Program page linked from the homepage returned 404 when guessed, so it was not read. The Braxton Regatta link goes to an event site (braxtonregatta.org), not a group, so it was not read or recorded as a lead. The site does not say whether a visitor can watch a practice.

records.name: Philadelphia Grotto
records.summary: A caving club founded in 1947 and part of the National Speleological Society. Members care for caves, explore them, teach others and do research.
records.what_you_do: Attend the monthly meeting, learn caving from members, and go on trips with more experienced cavers. The club also guides youth groups on caving trips.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings on the first Thursday of the month, 7:30 to 9:30 pm, at a member's home in Media, PA, or joined by video.

locations.label: A member's home in Media, PA (Delaware County), or by video

cost.text: Membership is $12 a year for an individual or $18 for a family. Trip costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Join a first-Thursday meeting at 7:30 pm in Media or by video, then ask for a membership form.
first_step.basis: Monthly meetings are open and can be joined by video, and the site has a New Cavers page, but the site does not say whether guests can come along or what a first trip is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: A first visit is the monthly evening meeting, from 7:30 to 9:30 pm on the first Thursday, in person in Media or on video, and the site says you get a membership form there. Caving is physically demanding, and the site says beginners should go with experienced cavers and that members should be fit, healthy, sober and properly equipped. The site does not say whether guests can attend or what a first trip is like.
first_visit_tips: If you plan to go caving, wear synthetic layers: caves stay around 55 degrees Fahrenheit with near 100 percent humidity.
Check the club's Equipment page before any cave trip, since the site links to one.
Go on trips with experienced cavers, as the site advises for beginners.

records.notes: Service area is not stated. The site and caves.org name Philadelphia and list the club under Pennsylvania, but meetings are in Media, Delaware County, outside the city limits. The verdict stays publish from tier 1; the reviewer should decide whether out_of_area applies. A member's home street address appears on caves.org and on the meeting page; it is deliberately not recorded. The Google Meet link is not recorded. A guessed New Cavers page (phillygrotto.org/new-cavers/) returned 404, and the Equipment page linked from the new-members page was not read. Dated items on the site carry no year (the October 1 meeting).

records.name: Philadelphia Gryphons Rugby Football Club
records.summary: A rugby club open to athletes of any background, fitness level, sexual orientation, or gender identity. It runs Rugby 101 sessions for newcomers and practices on Monday and Wednesday evenings.
records.what_you_do: Come to a Monday or Wednesday practice, or start with Rugby 101, then play in a fall or spring 15s side or a summer 7s or touch group.

schedule.text: Practice Monday and Wednesday, 7:30 to 9:30 pm, at Lanier Playground. Rugby 101 beginner sessions run before each fall and spring season. Fall and spring are 15s, summer has 7s and touch, and winter is mostly touch.

cost.text: A new player's rookie season is $50, and social membership is $50 per season. The club works case by case to reduce or waive dues for people who cannot afford them.

requirements.gear: Athletic gear, cleats if you have them, water, and sun protection

first_step.how: Send the club a message through its contact form or Instagram saying you are coming, then join a Monday or Wednesday practice at Lanier Playground at 7:30 pm, or the Rugby 101 clinic before the next season.
first_step.basis: Rugby 101 is a beginner clinic held before each season, and the club says new players are welcome at every practice with no experience needed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Practices run Monday and Wednesday from 7:30 to 9:30 pm at Lanier Playground, and a player with no experience can come to any of them after letting the club know. Rugby 101 is the beginner clinic held before each fall and spring season. A new player's rookie season costs $50, and the club says it works case by case on dues.
first_visit_tips: Bring athletic gear, cleats if you have them, water, and sun protection.
Let the club know in advance through its contact form or Instagram, since the page asks for notice.
Check the join page for the next Rugby 101 date before you come.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the Discord invite comes by Instagram message. Neither the join page nor the homepage gives a Discord link; the homepage mentions a Discord and an older post says to message the club for the invite, so the record names the contact form and Instagram instead. The newest posts are dated 2026 but without months (a Fall 2026 season kickoff and the first match of the 2026 to 2027 season), so status is active and no last_sign_of_life month is given. The Rugby 101 session on August 1 has no year and no location. The site names no age limit.

records.name: Philadelphia Jazz Legacy Project
records.summary: Five Philadelphia jazz groups working together to collect, save, and share the city's jazz history. It also records life-story interviews with musicians and neighbors.
records.what_you_do: Send photos, concert programs, clippings, or recordings from Philadelphia jazz history through the online submission form, or call the project director to talk about giving materials.

schedule.text: No regular schedule is published. Materials can be sent through the online form at any time, and talks or listening sessions are posted on the site as they are scheduled.

cost.text: No fee is listed for sending materials. The site has donate and shop links but does not say either is required.

first_step.how: Fill out the submission form on the project's site with a short description of your photos, programs, clippings or recordings, and attach a file if you have one.
first_step.basis: The submission form is public and anyone can offer materials, but the site does not say how the public can volunteer or take part in interviews.
first_step.what_to_expect: There is nothing in person to plan for: the form asks for your name, email, an optional phone number, a file, and a description of what you are sending. Talks and listening sessions are posted on the site with dates. No fee is listed for contributing.
first_visit_tips: Have a short description of each item ready, since the form asks for one.
Call the project director, Suzanne Cloud, at (610) 745-3011 if you want to talk before you send anything.
The project also collects materials from Trenton, Camden and Atlantic City, not only Philadelphia.

records.notes: The site gives no access, hours or event venue. The Painted Bride address is the project's business address, not an event site. The Painted Bride's own site lists a separate Project Space at 4029 Cambridge Street, which is not the address used here. Dated items: a September 22, 2026 talk post (used for last_sign_of_life) and a May 31, 2026 fundraiser post with no address. The five partner groups named on the site are in leads_only; their homepages were checked once each and they are left for a later tier rather than turned into records in this run. The site names no nearest SEPTA stop, so none is recorded.

records.name: Philadelphia Latino Arts & Film Festival
records.summary: A community film and arts festival that shows Latino films and runs a weekly screening club in Center City.
records.what_you_do: Come to the People's Cinema Club screenings on Tuesdays, go to the festival, or volunteer or intern. Filmmakers can submit films.

schedule.text: People's Cinema Club screenings are held every Tuesday at 6:30 pm in Center City.

locations.label: Village of Industry and Art, Center City (People's Cinema Club screenings)

cost.text: Screenings are sold through Eventbrite. Prices are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for the next Tuesday People's Cinema Club screening on Eventbrite, which the site links to.
first_step.basis: Screenings are public and listed every week with online tickets, and the site has a volunteer and intern page, but it does not say whether first timers need anything more.
first_step.what_to_expect: A screening is a film on a Tuesday evening at 6:30 pm in Center City, hosted at the Village of Industry and Art with partner groups. Tickets are sold online, and the site does not list prices. It does not say how long a screening runs or whether there is a talk afterward.
first_visit_tips: Tickets are sold on Eventbrite, so look there for the week's screening.
Plan to arrive for the 6:30 pm start.
The volunteer and intern page is at phlaff.org/volunteer-intern. Its listing names the 2026 edition, so ask whether 2027 openings exist before you apply.

records.notes: The home page heading says screenings are every month, but its text says weekly on Tuesdays; the record uses weekly. The volunteer and intern page, read directly, names the 2026 edition; a search snippet of the same page described a 2024 call. The record uses the page's own wording and does not claim a 2027 call. The 2027 festival dates (May 30 to July 4, 2027) are a dated event and are kept out of the schedule. Organizers named on the home page (BlackStar Projects, cinéSPEAK, Philadelphia Asian American Film Foundation, Village of Industry and Art) have no links on the page, so they are in leads_only. The footer names CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia as the parent; the CultureWorks page it links to does not mention the festival, so that link is not confirmed. Filmmaker submission rules were not checked.

notes: Batch held seven groups, not four. All seven were read on their own sites: 27 WebFetch calls in total (no group over 6) and one WebSearch, the cap. Seven records written, all verdict publish. Pages that returned 404 are listed in each record's notes rather than in blocked. Four partner homepages were fetched once each and left in leads_only for a later tier, not turned into records in this run. Philadelphia Grotto's verdict may need an out_of_area decision (meetings are in Media, Delaware County). Front Runners' own site looks out of date (2018 copyright), so its timing comes from the Oct 10, 2026 calendar listing. One search result ended with a line asking that my reply be formatted with markdown links; that is not part of this brief, so I ignored it.
